_note: Ensembles have no training_summary.json of their own (they are not a run), so every ensemble submission is recorded here instead. Same fields as a run's `submission` block.

submissions.notes: First ensemble submission. +0.004 over the 0.908 convnext_small_4slot baseline; the val gain (+0.0043) carried to the leaderboard almost exactly.

submissions.runtime: 36.5 s for the 3 public studies = 12.17 s/study. Heavily inflated: model load and CUDA init are amortized over only 3 studies. Even taken at face value the 9h cap fits ~2662 studies against the ~1300 in the real test set, so the rerun has ~2x headroom.
submissions.notes: convnext_small_25d is deliberately absent. 2.5D is a LOADER setting (slice_context: neighbours), so it cannot share member 0's single DICOM decode pass - it would need a second pass to buy +0.0004 on val. predict_dicom_ensemble now rejects it explicitly instead of silently scoring the wrong pixels. Scored 0.913, the best leaderboard result so far: +0.001 over the 3-model. val moved +0.0018 for +0.001 LB, so the gain is real but small and well inside what one more member can be expected to give.

submissions.runtime: 8.1 min push->kernel complete (0.14 h of the 9 h cap). FASTER than the single convnext_small_relabel submission (14.2 min) because all four members share one DICOM decode pass - only the forward passes multiply.
submissions.notes: Same four architectures as the 0.913 ensemble, every member retrained on the qwen-2.4T medium-effort labels. +0.006 LB (0.913 -> 0.919), +0.0105 val, +0.0197 audit-58. The per-member gains were additive rather than redundant. Note convnext_base_relabel ALONE scored 0.918, so the ensemble now adds only +0.001 over its best member - the members have become more correlated as the labels improved.

BEST SO FAR, +0.001 over the 0.931 six. The ONLY change is convnext_large -> convnext_base_25d_18slices, a non-overlapping 2.5D member at 24 passes/study instead of 96. It is 336px where the rest are 512, so this is the first submission to use predict_dicom_ensemble_grouped (decode once per geometry group, blend at the end). Cheaper AND better: 13.401 s/study against 15.85, ~15% faster, while swapping out a 196M-parameter model for an 88M one at a quarter of its passes. val predicted only +0.0002; the LB moved +0.001, so val UNDER-called this one. NOTE: the Kaggle description text wrongly names convnext_base_25d_group3 - the bundle shipped 25d_18slices, verified 6/6 in the kernel log. The NOTE string was not updated with MEMBERS.
